24.0.0.en: Christ sat with His disciples on the Mount of Olives, which is near Jerusalem, and from there the Temple is clearly visible. The disciples asked Christ about the time of the destruction of the Temple, and they also asked Him about His second coming, and what the signs are that appear before His coming, so that they might take heed and be prepared.

24.0.1.en: From this it appears that Christ's answer includes two subjects, namely the destruction of Jerusalem and His second coming. We shall notice their overlapping, because the lesson drawn from them is one, namely repentance and preparation. The Jews used to think that their Temple would remain until the end of days, and the disciples thought that its destruction would be at the end.

24.1.0.en: Christ warned them of the appearance of false pretenders, each of whom says that he is the Christ, or who come as though they were messengers from Him; so they must be examined, and one must not be led after them. And if they do not say words that agree with the word of the Holy Bible and the Church, they are liars, so we reject them.

24.1.1.en: Do not rush toward any teachings outside the Church, even if the one who speaks them has a name and fame, but stand firm in your Church and its teachings, and by prayer and submission to the guidance of your spiritual fathers, you will discover the error in the teachings of strangers.

24.2.0.en: Satan stirs people up against one another, so divisions and wars occur, in order that they hate one another, so that he may dominate them and occupy them with problems away from the worship of God, and fill them with anxiety and fear.

24.2.1.en: "Be not troubled": do not be alarmed by these reports, but expect them, and pray that God may support you and give you peace, and keep those who are within these wars.

24.2.2.en: "But the end is not yet": these wars remind you to prepare for the end of days, but they are not the final sign before the Day of Judgment.

24.3.0.en: A second sign that Christ gives is not only divisions and wars, but lack of food and drink, that is, famines, so that many die. Then Satan spreads diseases as epidemics, to frighten people and distract them from God. And he uses another sign, namely earthquakes and all changes in nature, so that people murmur against God.

24.4.0.en: All these signs will recur many times, but they are the beginning of sorrows, and there are still other signs before the coming of Christ.

24.4.1.en: Do not be alarmed if afflictions face you, but trust in the power of your God to protect you from the wars of the devil, and to turn the material affliction into growth in your spiritual life; only hold fast to God with prayers and faithfulness in your life.

24.5.0.en: Besides the general calamities by which the devil tries to make them fall into murmuring, he stirs up afflictions against the children of God in many persecutions for the sake of their faith, so they lose much of the comfort of the body, and are even exposed to torments that reach death; and by this he tries to keep them away from God, and even to deny Christ.

24.6.0.en: In the face of the persecutions that confront the children of God, some believers fear and doubt, so they apostatize from the faith and resist their brethren, and ally with the wicked to persecute the believers, so they deliver them to wicked rulers to be punished and killed, and by this divisions and hatred occur between those who apostatize from the faith and their believing brethren, and they even become more persecuting of their brethren than the outside persecutors.

24.6.1.en: Look to your Christ, who endured many sufferings unto death, that you may accept afflictions for His sake. And do not be disturbed if those nearest to you resist you, but stand firm in your love for God and for them, and pray for them that they may return to the faith, confident that God supports you, so that no one harms you except by His permission.

24.7.0.en: The third blow that Satan directs at the children of God, after the general calamities and the particular afflictions, is to lead them astray from the truth by the appearance of many false prophets, that is, people who claim to be sent by God, or the holders of philosophies and doctrines that draw people away and make them doubt God and the Church, and make them fall into various desires.

24.8.0.en: By people's departure from God and their falling into many desires, their love for God grows weak, and they become carnal and far from the spiritual life.

24.9.0.en: On the other side, a few hold fast to the right faith, and reject the pressures of doubt and deception. And whoever remains steadfast declares his faith and his love, and receives eternal salvation.

24.10.0.en: So that man may be without excuse, God provides the call to the right faith to all mankind, so the preaching reaches everyone before the second coming of Christ, to give the opportunity of salvation to all.

24.10.1.en: Do not be led after any strange teachings or meetings outside the Church, and be careful in your friendships so as to keep your right faith.

24.11.0.en: If the Christians notice the siege of Jerusalem, whether those who are in it or in the land of Judea surrounding it, let them flee to the mountains around them so that the Roman soldiers do not destroy them. And indeed, those who remained in Jerusalem were killed by Titus, the Roman commander, in very great numbers.

24.12.0.en: If a person is on the housetop, let him flee quickly when he sees the Roman soldiers approaching from afar, and not think of his belongings that are in the house, so that he may escape with his life.

24.13.0.en: Those working in the fields must run swiftly forward, and not return even to take their clothes that they had taken off to do their work.

24.14.0.en: The difficulty of flight is evident for pregnant women and nursing mothers who carry the unborn and small children, because they are weighed down by what they carry.

24.15.0.en: Would that this destruction and the flight from it not be in winter, so that the rains would not hinder the flight and the roads would not be muddy, and also not on a Sabbath, so that their conscience would not trouble them that they are running long distances on the Sabbath day against what the Law commands, or so that the Jewish police would not prevent them from that.

24.15.1.en: And from the spiritual side, all the above signifies fleeing quickly from evil to the mountains, which indicate rising with God above the world, and not descending to desires or falling back to them, and seeking God's help to support our weakness if we are weighed down by the burdens and labors of this world.

24.15.2.en: Let us hasten to flee, caring for the salvation of our souls before everything, and giving up material things that we may receive the Kingdom.

24.16.0.en: The attack of Titus the Roman on Jerusalem was violent, and he killed in it more than a million Jews, in addition to those he killed in Judea; there had been no destruction like it in all this region. "Such as was not since the beginning ... no, nor ever shall be": that is, no destruction this cruel had occurred in Jerusalem, and none will occur afterward to this extent.

24.16.1.en: And this signifies the great tribulation that will occur in the whole world before the Day of Judgment, such as there was not before, nor ever shall be.

24.17.0.en: God intervened, so the siege of Jerusalem lasted only five months, so that all who were in it would not perish. God did this so that the Christians would flee to the mountains as He had told them.

24.17.1.en: This also applies to the end of days, when there will be severe persecution from Satan against the children of God so that they turn back from their faith, and he will press them hard even in obtaining the necessities of life, and torture and kill many. But the love of God will make this period short, so that the faith of His children does not weaken and they do not deny their Christ, but He permits afflictions in proportion to the endurance of His children, and gives them help to flee from them, and to take refuge in the Church and spiritual worship, and so find their salvation.

24.17.2.en: Be reassured, for God does not let you be tempted above your strength, and He supports you in affliction, and even makes it a motive for your drawing near to Him; so trust that the hand of God, the Pantocrator, your heavenly Father, directs your life and nothing harms you.

24.18.s.en: (9) The second coming is announced to all

24.18.0.en: Christ warns His children of the appearance of wicked people who claim to be He, and pretend to piety, but slip in strange teachings to lead the believers astray. So one must keep away from them and reject their teachings as long as they are outside the Church, whatever their miracles, for Satan is able to do miracles, but they are not constructive. And as long as a person is obedient to the Church and her fathers, there is no fear for him of going astray.

24.19.0.en: Part of the deception is the claim that the coming and appearance of Christ will be to a few in some place, such as a certain desert, or hidden in a closed place with a special group; so Christ warns that His coming will be announced to all mankind at the same time.

24.20.0.en: Christ gives a comparison for His coming with the lightning that appears in the sky, which all people see, whether in the east or the west; thus no one needs to warn another of the coming of Christ. It is to be noted that lightning appears suddenly and is clear to all who look, and thus will be the second coming of Christ.

24.21.0.en: This verse can be meant of the destruction of Jerusalem, for the carcase is the Jewish nation that had departed from God, so it became dead to Him, and the Romans fell upon it like eagles and destroyed Jerusalem, and they carried their emblem, which is the eagles, on their standards as they attacked Jerusalem.

24.21.1.en: This verse also applies to the end of days, when the eagles, who are the angels, swoop upon the wicked, who are signified by the carcase, to declare God's wrath and judgment on them, to cast them into eternal torment. Likewise, the carcase is meant of the crucified Christ, who is given on the altar in His Church every day as true Body and Blood; there the saints gather, who are raised up in a heavenly life like eagles flying in the height of heaven. Thus at the coming of Christ, His children gather around Him by means of the angels, and rejoice with Him. And on the contrary, the wicked gather around the devil in eternal torment.

24.21.2.en: If you are like the eagle, one of the children of God, your place of gathering is around Christ in the Church, and you will always find your rest and your joy.

24.22.0.en: Christ continues His talk about the Day of Judgment, for after the collapse of nature, the sign of the Son of man appears in heaven, which is the Cross, with light and glory. Then all the unbelievers and the unrepentant tremble and are put to shame, because they refused to believe in the crucified Christ, and even crucified Him many times in their lives by their immersion in evil, and they mourn in remorse without hope. And He calls them "the tribes of the earth", to distinguish them from the heavenly children of God who believe in Him. Then Christ Himself appears in great glory on the clouds of heaven, because we have become accustomed that the cloud indicates the presence of God, as happened in the days of Moses and at the Transfiguration.

24.22.1.en: And His appearance in His glory is utterly different from the image of His humility at His first coming in the flesh.

24.23.0.en: The angels of God appear at once with trumpets of shouting, joy and victory, to gather the children of God who believe in Him from the four corners of the world, to reign forever with their Christ. They gather not only the dwellers of heaven, that is, the spirits of the saints, but all those who lived a heavenly life on earth.

24.23.1.en: How great and joyful is that day for the children of God! Let us prepare with repentance and great exactness, and endure the sufferings of life that we may be glorified with Him.

24.24.s.en: (12) The parable of the fig tree

24.24.0.en: Christ gives a parable here, namely the fig tree, which appears dry in the winter season, but when summer comes the sap flows in its branches, and it is filled with leaves, blossoms and fruit, and this is evidence of the arrival of the summer season.

24.24.1.en: Likewise, if the signs previously mentioned in this chapter (vv. 5-15) appear, this means that the destruction of Jerusalem is near.

24.24.2.en: If evil increases and you endure many afflictions, this means that the relief of the affliction is near, and God's glorifying you.

24.25.0.en: "This generation": a generation includes from 30 to 40 years, and the destruction of Jerusalem occurred forty years after these words, and some of the hearers lived until the destruction of Jerusalem, such as John the Beloved. Christ specifies the time of the fulfilment of these signs, which is the generation in which those who hear Him live, and He means the destruction of Jerusalem in AD 70.

24.25.1.en: He also means the spread of faith in Him in the continents known at that time, and the beginning of the believers' preparation for the eternal Kingdom.

24.26.s.en: (13) The time of the coming of Christ

24.26.0.en: Christ affirms the truth of His words and the certainty of their fulfilment, for they are more steadfast than anything known to mankind.

24.26.1.en: For though the earth is firm under their feet, and the heaven is high above them, they will pass away on the Day of Judgment, so that the word of God may be fulfilled, and He takes His children into His Kingdom. And heaven signifies the spirit that goes to it, and earth the body that is laid in it. That is, people die over the course of generations, but in the end these signs and His second coming must be fulfilled.

24.27.0.en: No one must be occupied with fixing the time of His coming, for He will not announce it even to His angels, so that people do not grow slack in their striving and spiritual preparation, or tremble and fear so that their spiritual movement is paralyzed. Since God will not announce the time of His coming, nor the day of your departure from the world, you must prepare every day with repentance, prayer and love for others.

24.28.s.en: (14) Preparing for the coming of Christ

24.28.0.en: He gives a comparison for our present life in which we prepare for the coming of Christ, with what happened in the days of Noah. For before the flood, people were occupied with their desires and material affairs, marrying, eating and drinking, forgetting their relationship with God and repentance for their sins. Likewise now in our life, there are many who are occupied with their worldly concerns away from the salvation of their souls.

24.29.0.en: The flood came suddenly, and because they were not prepared they perished.

24.29.1.en: Likewise the coming of Christ comes suddenly, and only those prepared by a life of repentance are saved.

24.30.0.en: People will be mingled together in their living in one family or work or neighborhood, but some of them care about preparing for eternity, and the other is absorbed in his desires, refusing repentance. Then the one is taken to the heavenly glories, and the other is left to be cast into eternal torment.

24.30.1.en: Do not be absorbed in material preoccupations, for they are not the goal of your life, but the goal is the love of God. So accustom yourself to a relationship with Him in prayers, fasts and spiritual readings, so that if the day of the end surprises you, you will be at rest, indeed glorified with joy unspeakable.

24.31.s.en: (15) The parable of the goodman of the house and the thief

24.31.0.en: Christ continues His talk about preparation for the Kingdom, and proclaims openly the importance of spiritual watchfulness, that is, vigilance and attention to the salvation of the soul by repentance, and examining oneself every day, and caring for spiritual practices, that our love for God may grow, and from it result love, forgiveness and service to others. And the reason for His emphasis on the importance of watchfulness, that is, constant preparation, is our not knowing the time of His coming.

24.32.0.en: "Watch": a division of the night, which the Jews divide into four divisions.

24.32.1.en: "The thief": death, and also a figure of the sudden coming of the Son of man.

24.32.3.en: "In an hour when ye think not": in an hour you do not know.

24.32.4.en: Christ gives a parable about the importance of spiritual watchfulness to face the thief (death), who comes during the night, seizing the opportunity of the sleep of those in the house to break in and enter from any place to rob it. If the goodman of the house, who is responsible for it, knew the time of the thief's coming, he would stay awake to prevent him from robbing his house.

24.32.5.en: Then He affirms the importance of preparation, because Christ has not and will not specify the time of His coming.

24.32.6.en: Be careful lest Satan direct your thought and senses toward evil desires until he persuades you of their necessity, and you are surprised by the Day of Judgment and cannot do anything.

24.33.s.en: (16) The parable of the faithful servant

24.33.0.en: Christ presents another parable of a master who appoints one of his servants as steward for him to care for the needs of those working for him, and travels for a time. Then He asks about the qualities of the faithful and wise servant, and answers that he is the one who gives food to all in the house at the right time.

24.33.1.en: "The servant": every Christian: a father or mother or servant responsible for shepherding and serving others.

24.33.2.en: "Faithful": he who fulfils his duties in the fullest way.

24.33.3.en: "Wise": he who prepares for his eternity by spiritual watchfulness.

24.33.5.en: "His household": all the souls surrounding the Christian or servant, whom God requires him to shepherd and care for spiritually.

24.33.6.en: "Meat": spiritual care, and what it also includes of meeting material and psychological needs. "In due season": that is, at the right time when they need it.

24.34.0.en: He commends the servant who does what his master charged him with throughout the period of his journey, and rewards him by appointing him steward over all his possessions.

24.34.1.en: And by this he signifies the importance of each one's care for the salvation of his own soul, and the satisfying of his spirit and body by a living relationship with God, and his caring also for serving all those around him and drawing souls to Christ. And the reward is that He raises him to heaven to give him the knowledge of God, and constant enjoyment of fellowship with Him.

24.34.2.en: "When his lord cometh": the coming of Christ on the Day of Judgment.

24.34.3.en: "So doing": continuing in his faithfulness and spiritual vigilance and preparation for eternity.

24.34.4.en: "Verily": an affirmation of the importance of what He is about to declare.

24.34.5.en: "All his goods": that is, the knowledge of God in eternity and the enjoyment of fellowship with Him.

24.35.0.en: The unfaithful servant behaves in evil after being appointed steward to care for the servants in the house, so instead of caring for their needs, he is harsh to them, thinking that his master will not come soon. And he is absorbed in satisfying his material pleasures, which are represented by eating and drinking wine to drunkenness.

24.35.1.en: "That evil servant": the Christian or servant who neglects his relationship with God and is occupied with evil desires. "Delayeth his coming": he forgets the preparation for the day of the Lord on the pretext that there is still a long time in life, so he plunges into desires.

24.35.2.en: "Smite his fellowservants": cruelty and injustice in treating others.

24.35.3.en: "Eat and drink with the drunken": absorption in pleasures and material desires.

24.36.1.en: "That servant": the selfish person occupied with his corrupt desires, who has no love toward others, and ignores preparing for his eternity.

24.36.2.en: "Cut him asunder": that is, destroy him.

24.36.3.en: The master comes suddenly without appointment, and sees the unfaithfulness of his servant in his service, so he destroys him and casts him with the wicked hypocrites into eternal torment where there is weeping and gnashing of teeth, that is, very severe pains and despair, because he pretends to be a steward for God in caring for himself and those around him, while in truth he corrupts himself and wrongs others. Examine the responsibilities and the souls among whom God has placed you, to draw them to Him, and ask yourself how faithful you are with your time and talents and all your abilities, and have you used them for the glory of God or for your personal mood and turned aside with them into evil?

24.36.4.en: And do you pray and strive for the salvation of every soul around you?

24.36.5.en: Chapter twenty-five: the parables of the virgins and the talents; the work of mercy
